effect: Adding white cells and platelets completed the blood and the chapter. The final picture distinguishes oxygen carried in red cells from nutrients dissolved in plasma.
reaction: Seeing the components together made their different transport roles clearer, though the white cells' and platelets' jobs were only briefly explained.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding oxygen to red cells was most worthwhile: the picture showed that oxygen can both attach to haemoglobin and be released near tissues.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding red cells to plasma felt mostly like an assembly step; the following unfilled outlines made the final addition predictable.

surprise.text: I noticed that mature red cells have no nuclei, even though the developing cells started with them.

arbitrary.text: No action felt completely arbitrary, but adding white cells and platelets was guided mainly by the goal and outlines; their specific jobs were explained only after adding them.

continue.text: I would probably continue: the clear pictures linking blood components to what they carry made me curious about where the blood goes next, although some assembly steps were predictable.
